case_reviews.statement: IRGC said two U.S. destroyers were struck and heavily damaged.
case_reviews.counterevidence: CENTCOM publicly said no U.S. Navy warship was struck and IRGC attempts failed.
case_reviews.action: Cross-check already sealed verdict, sources, corrections and knowledge before any re-adjudication; do not insert another unique proposition.

case_reviews.statement: Iranian Navy (regular Artesh Navy), in a statement carried by IRNA, claimed to have destroyed an unidentified 'enemy unmanned vessel' east of the Strait of Hormuz; the claim did not identify vessel operator or class.
case_reviews.counterevidence: CENTCOM: all U.S. military unmanned surface vessels in Middle East accounted for. Relevant to US-asset interpretation; not affirmative disproof of an unspecified enemy unmanned vessel.
case_reviews.needed: Original IRNA/Farsi transcript and speaker military service; claimed target identity or wreckage; independent evidence of destruction; whether Iranian 'enemy' means U.S. vessel in context; reconcile original case CF-20261030-03 actor and proposition scope.
case_reviews.original_statement_actor: Iranian regular Navy, not established as IRGC Navy
case_reviews.source_fidelity_correction: The Oct30 original Iranian Navy statement did NOT explicitly identify the destroyed unmanned vessel as U.S.-operated. CENTCOM replied that all U.S. military unmanned surface vessels were accounted for. That refutes a U.S.-vessel version but does not alone falsify the original unspecified-operator statement. In the same reporting, the separate IRGC Navy statement concerned two stopped tankers, NOT the unmanned vessel.

case_reviews.statement: IRGC claimed it had shot down the 56th U.S. MQ-9 drone.
case_reviews.specificity: 56th of exact aircraft model, not a fungible cumulative all-drone count.
case_reviews.needed: IRGC individual 1–56 log; distinguish MQ-1/MQM-170/MQ-9, duplicate photos, loss dates, U.S. admissions, distinct November hull ID and authenticated imagery.
case_reviews.note: CRS had >=45 MQ-9 losses by Aug. 13; this does not by itself falsify an alleged 56th by November.

case_reviews.statement: IRGC said four tankers were destroyed by naval mines while using prohibited southern Hormuz route.
case_reviews.needed: Names/IMO numbers and casualty/disablement evidence for each hull; separate limpet mine from anchored mine, stopped vs burned vs destroyed, and confirm no double count with Oct. 29–30 reports.

case_reviews.statement: Unnamed IRGC Navy official said no unauthorized vessels transited the Strait overnight after navigation aids were destroyed.
case_reviews.needed: Exact overnight clock, scope of 'unauthorized', ship/voyage identifiers, AIS and port/UKMTO corroboration and source of destroyed-aids claim.

next_action: Only Claims Forensics can authorize fresh atomized FALSE and knowledge verdicts. Do not convert denied or unsupported propositions into Lie-count increments without an evidentiary judgment under controlling contract.

source_fidelity_correction.finding: Oct30 unmanned vessel allegation belongs to regular Iranian Navy in the available IRNA-attributed report, while IRGC Navy's Oct30 claim concerned tanker passage/stoppage.
source_fidelity_correction.prior_index_issue: Actor and operator in that case may be over-specified as IRGC and U.S.; re-open original wording attribution before any final truth or knowledge judgment.
